How did a lake kill 1,800 people overnight?
In 1986 a quiet lake killed almost 1,800 people in one evening. No wave, no fire, just gas 🫧 How Lake Nyos became a shaken soda bottle, in 8-bit.

scenes.title: A LAKE KILLED 1,800
vo: In nineteen eighty-six, a quiet lake killed almost eighteen hundred people in one evening.
No wave. No fire. So how?

scenes.title: LEVEL 1
vo: Fifty miles down, magma leaks carbon dioxide.
It seeps up into the lake's deepest water.

scenes.title: LEVEL 2
vo: Down there, the water's weight squeezes the gas in, like a soda cap.
The deep layer never mixes with the top, so the gas keeps building.

scenes.title: LEVEL 3
vo: On August twenty-first, that deep water rose. The pressure dropped, and the gas burst out at once.
Nobody knows exactly what tipped it.

scenes.title: LEVEL 4
vo: Carbon dioxide is heavier than air, so it poured downhill,
at over sixty miles an hour.

scenes.title: THE ANSWER
vo: It pushed away the air people breathed.
Nearly eighteen hundred people suffocated, and thirty-five hundred animals.

scenes.title: AFTERMATH
vo: Since two thousand one, pipes let the gas out slowly, so it can't build up again.
Today about ten thousand people live there again.

scenes.title: SAVE POINT
vo: The quietest lake can be the deadliest.
